headline: Committee advances license plate reader rules, delays facial recognition bill

meeting.body: Maui County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee
meeting.summary: The committee voted 7 to 1 to recommend passing Bill 113 on license plate reader data and deferred Bill 112 on facial recognition.
meeting.recap: The committee reconvened on September 3 to continue its meeting from September 2.[[0:00:29]] Oral public testimony was closed, but written testimony was still being accepted.[[0:05:37]] Two bills were on the agenda: Bill 113 on license plate reader data and Bill 112 on facial recognition technology.[[0:05:51]] A police lieutenant said 27 license plate reader cameras came bundled with 400 radios in a 2025 Motorola contract.[[0:09:57]] Police said the department owns the camera data and Motorola cannot access it.[[0:13:06]] A police lieutenant said 11 cameras helped solve at least 40 cases in about a year.[[0:49:35]] Police said the current cameras take photos and cannot take live video.[[0:55:29]] Police said every search of the system is logged, dated and timed.[[0:57:08]] Members passed an amendment, eight to zero, so the County must not sign or renew a license plate reader contract with certain vendors.[[1:51:18]] Council Member Johnson cast the no vote.[[2:04:35]] The committee deferred, or put off, Bill 112 with no objections.[[2:24:51]]
meeting.next: Committee staff will send a follow-up letter for the exact yearly camera license costs. Police said they would check their records and report back case numbers tied to the cameras. The chair said the South Maui Community Plan will pause other committee work for about a month. A police lieutenant suggested demonstrations and discussion with members before any decision on facial recognition.
